system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Great-Power Rivalry, Regional Wars and an AI-Driven Economic Shock
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system where renewed great-power competition, localized wars, and a technology-led capital boom are mutually amplifying risks. Regional conflicts (Iran/Hormuz, Israel–Gaza/Lebanon, Russia–Ukraine) are disrupting trade, energy and sea lanes while tempering allied coordination; simultaneously an AI and semiconductor race is reshaping supply chains, investment flows and industrial policy. Financial markets and trade (bond yields, tariffs, commodity prices, shipping chokepoints) are transmitting shocks quickly across the system, creating feedback loops that can cascade between military, economic and technological subsystems.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and their alliances, regional conflict zones, global trade and shipping routes, multinational tech and energy firms, financial markets (bonds, commodities, FX), and strategic industrial supply chains (AI, semiconductors, shipping)
system_description.super_system: Planetary human system of political-economic-technological order (global international system embedded in the wider socio-economic and ecological context)
adjacent_subsystems: Middle East maritime-security and Iran conflict subsystem (Hormuz, Gulf states, Houthi strikes)
Eurasian landwar and great-power competition subsystem (Russia–Ukraine, Russia–North Korea ties)
Global technology and industrial subsystem (AI race, semiconductors, supply-chain reconfiguration)
International financial and trade subsystem (bond markets, tariffs, commodity and FX shocks)

variables.name: Strait of Hormuz crisis
variables.description: The United States, Iran, Gulf states and regional proxies are contesting control of the Strait of Hormuz and nearby sea lanes as ship attacks, a de‑facto blockade and stalled ceasefire diplomacy escalate economic pressure and threaten energy flows.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a protracted and evolving war, with increasing use of long‑range drones and strikes on Black Sea ports reshaping battlefield tactics, logistics and the scope of Western support and sanctions.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are escalating a strategic rivalry through tariffs, export controls and supply‑chain manoeuvres that are rewiring global manufacturing, market access and trade relationships for advanced hardware.

variables.name: AI capital concentration and governance
variables.description: Major tech firms, global investors and regulators are driving a rapid concentration of AI compute, talent and financing that is shifting corporate power, IPO and funding dynamics and provoking new regulatory and governance battles worldwide.

variables.name: Alliance credibility in Asia‑Pacific
variables.description: U.S. policy choices and partner reactions across East Asia — especially involving South Korea and Japan — are testing alliance cohesion as changes to military exercises, deterrence postures and burden‑sharing recalibrate regional security commitments.
